messages:
maria_support: Heads-up — ClearLedger reported a spike of 5xx/504s from hosted inference starting ~07:35 UTC. They see gateway 504s and client-side "request timed out". I attached the customer request IDs in the ticket.
kevin_oncall: @maria_support can you paste one of the request IDs + any associated route/model? I’ll start checking ingress metrics.
maria_support: request ids: cl-req-20260305-01 / cl-req-20260305-28. Route: /v1/generate hosted-model=rwd-compat-7b. Customer says most calls are long-context (>=12k tokens) and some batch-merge requests.
jordan_sre: seeing a correlated spike in request_queue_depth and dequeue_latency on cluster us-east-1c starting 07:33 UTC. p95 dequeue latency jumped from 12ms -> 1.8s, and tail p99 -> 12s. Also a small increase in continous-batcher backlog.
alex_runtime: that timing matches a canary push at 07:30 by deploy-bot. Looking at runtime logs: a handful of worker pods started warming KV cache for long contexts and blocked the batchers. snippet:
```
2026-03-05T07:31:12Z runtime[worker-42] INFO warming kv-cache seq=1..2048
2026-03-05T07:32:03Z batcher[batcher-9] WARN dequeue blocked awaiting kv init
2026-03-05T07:33:15Z gateway ERROR downstream timeout after 30s: no response
```
lisa_support: customer repro steps: they sent 3 parallel requests with context=14k each, 2 of them got 504s, one succeeded after 29s. Customer is on Dedicated->Hosted migration path so sensitive.
kevin_oncall: digging into ingress logs — I see many small requests concatenated into big continuous-batcher groups because the runtime is prioritizing long-cached KV warmups. Queue depth reached configured soft limit of 8192 and we started early rejections around 07:36.
maria_support: they quoted SLA complaints. They want ETA and mitigation.
jordan_sre: short-term mitigation: bump ingress dequeue workers on affected pool and enable aggressive preemption for cold-kv warmups. I can toggle preemption for us-east-1c, but it will increase p50 latency for warmup requests.
alex_runtime: patch ready to soft-limit per-tenant continuous-batcher window and to keep long-context warmups on separate warmup lane. Can flip a feature-flag but needs a quick canary.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout of rwd-compat-7b-20260305a -> 10% started at 07:30 UTC. 07:34 UTC observed scaled pods 4->9.
kevin_oncall: Action plan: 1) pause canary (deploy-bot) 2) enable preemption for kv-warmups in pool 7 3) increase dequeue parallelism by +2 on us-east-1c 4) vendor message to ClearLedger. I'll start 1 & 3 now.
kevin_oncall: (done) paused canary and bumped dequeue parallelism. monitoring now.
jordan_sre: metrics: dequeue latency p95 dropping back to 220ms within 90s. queue_depth trending down. early rejects cleared. gateway 504s tailing off.
lisa_support: informed customer — they acknowledged mitigation and asked for root-cause postmortem and permanent fix ETA.\nmaria_support: noted. Please keep thread updated. Also need reproduction snippet for eng:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY'
 -d '{"model":"rwd-compat-7b","input":"<14k tokens payload>","stream":false}'
```
alex_runtime: I'll run internal repro and exercise batcher warmup lane. If I can reproduce locally, I’ll push the warmup-lane switch and queue soft-limits change to prod next week.
jordan_sre: follow-ups: create incident ticket, collect kube pod restarts, and gather KV cache init timings per pod. Assigning to alex_runtime for root cause and to kevin_oncall for short-term infra changes.
maria_support: thanks — customer is on watch. Closing loop once we have RCA doc + postmortem.
